lesson.title: External, middle and inner ear
lesson.summary: The external acoustic meatus conducts sound to the tympanic membrane.

steps.title: CN VIII Vestibulocochlear Nerve
steps.body: The vestibulocochlear nerve is special sensory for hearing and balance. It has cochlear and vestibular components entering the brainstem at the cerebellopontine angle after passing through internal acoustic meatus.

steps.title: Relationships and functional organization
steps.body: Cochlear component carries hearing from organ of Corti to spiral ganglion and cochlear nuclei. Vestibular component carries balance from semicircular ducts, utricle, and saccule to vestibular ganglion and vestibular nuclei. Travels with facial nerve through internal acoustic meatus. Lesions may produce sensorineural hearing loss, tinnitus, vertigo, dizziness, or balance disturbance. Cerebellopontine angle tumors can affect VII and VIII together.

steps.title: How does conductive hearing loss differ anatomically from sensorineural loss?
steps.body: Conductive loss concerns transmission through external or middle-ear structures, such as the tympanic membrane or ossicular chain. Sensorineural loss involves cochlear sensory mechanisms or neural pathways, including CN VIII. The auditory tube ventilates the middle-ear cavity but is not the route carrying auditory nerve signals. Vestibular structures share the inner ear and VIII association yet encode balance-related information. Similar location does not make hearing and balance the same sensory system or imply that every ear problem affects both equally.

steps.title: Apply the anatomy and resolve a common confusion
steps.body: The external acoustic meatus conducts sound to the tympanic membrane. Malleus, incus and stapes transmit vibration through the middle ear to the oval window; round-window movement accommodates inner-ear fluid displacement. The auditory tube connects middle ear to nasopharynx. The cochlea encodes sound, while semicircular ducts detect angular acceleration and utricle and saccule detect linear acceleration and head tilt. CN VIII carries sensory information; it is not the motor nerve to middle-ear muscles.
